QuestionStmt.S: For an ideal gas, the density of the gas is $\rho_0$ when temperature and pressure of the gas are $T_0$ and $P_0$ respectively. When the temperature of the gas is $2T_0$, its pressure becomes $3P_0$. The new density will be

Solution.S:
Using $PV = nRT$ and $\rho = \frac{m}{V}$:

$$\rho \propto \frac{P}{T}$$

$$\rho = \rho_0 \times \frac{P}{P_0} \times \frac{T_0}{T} = \rho_0 \times \frac{3P_0}{P_0} \times \frac{T_0}{2T_0} = \frac{3}{2} \rho_0$$

Thus the correct option is D: $\frac{3}{2} \rho_0$.
